newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weak yen drives up Nissan parent profits.
newsitem.headline: Weak yen drives up Nissan parent profits.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd on Tuesday joined the list of Japanese car giants which have posted windfall profits from the weaker yen, saying its parent company profit more than doubled in the last business year.

The nation's second-biggest automaker said parent current profit totalled 81.03 billion yen ($698 million) in the year which ended in March, 2.5 times as much as in the previous year, as the weak yen made its products more competitive abroad.
Nissan also zoomed back into profit on a group basis, landing in the black for the first time in five years.

It posted a group net profit of 77.74 billion yen ($670 million) in 1996/97 after a net loss of 88.42 billion yen ($762 million) the previous year. Net profit is equal to current profit, which is pre-tax, minus taxes and extraordinary profits and losses.
Other car giants like Toyota Motor Corp and Honda Motor Co Ltd announced last week that their annual profits had soared to record levels as they reaped the benefit of the yen's weakness.

But Japanese carmakers, including Nissan, have predicted that their profit growth will be less dramatic this year. Nissan predicted a rise of about 36 percent in its parent-only profit and said it was aiming for a group net profit of more than 100 billion yen ($862 million) for 1997/98. ($1=116 yen)
